newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Chile's Infisa buys Banco Consolidado stake.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Infisa buys Banco Consolidado stake.

text.p: Chilean financial group Infisa bought an 80 percent share in Venezuela's fourth largest bank Banco Consolidado for $123.5 million in auction on Thursday, national State Deposits Guarantee Fund Fogade president Esther de Margulis said.
Infisa, which is Chile's largest pension fund manager, was the only bidder for the 80 percent share in the bank, whose base price had been set at $118.4 million.

Margulis said at the public presentation of the bidding results that local investors had also placed orders for some eight percent of the bank, worth five billion bolivars ($10.5 million), of the 20 percent offered.
The base price of the whole bank was originally set at $148 million.
"We believe there are excellent opportunites here in Venezuela's financial sector," Infisa representative Manuel Balbontin said.
"Our entry, along with Santander's, will prove a great advance for the sector as a whole and also the Venezuelan consumer," he added.
Earlier Thursday, Fogade sold a 90 percent share in Banco de Venezuela to Spain's Banco Santander SA for $338.4 million. ((-- John Paul Rathbone, Caracas newsroom, 582 505 2600))
